thread:
Gwen Park: Quick flag from customer Meridian - they see April embeddings ~6% lower vs their exporter. Sent csv with 12 request_ids.
Rico Alvarez: Thanks Gwen. Region? Any recent infra churn?
Gwen Park: ap-southeast-1, shared pool. We had a janitor job (cleanup-old-logs) rolled Apr 14 that touched the exporter retention policy.
Maya Patel: I ran a diff between exporter_events and billing_events for their sample. Many requests show exporter_vectors present but billing shows 0 for same request_id.
LedgerJanitor: Alert: 460 events for customer_meridian between 2026-04-14T02:00Z and 2026-04-14T04:30Z marked as DROPPED_BY_JANITOR.
Rico Alvarez: Ouch. Can you paste the grep and SQL you used?
Maya Patel: Grep: `grep meridian /var/log/janitor/2026-04-14*.log | head` shows cleanup entries removing `exporter_payload` keys older than 48h. SQL:

```
SELECT me.request_id, ee.exporter_vectors, be.billed_vectors, me.reason
FROM metering_events me
LEFT JOIN exporter_events ee ON me.request_id = ee.request_id
LEFT JOIN billing_events be ON me.request_id = be.request_id
WHERE me.customer_id='customer_meridian' AND me.event_time BETWEEN '2026-04-14' AND '2026-04-15'
AND me.reason = 'dropped_by_janitor';
```

Results: exporter_vectors present in EE but billing_event shows billed_vectors=0 and reason=dropped_by_janitor.
Gwen Park: How many tokens impacted?
Maya Patel: Aggregate: ~520k vectors -> ~$260 list / ~$180 committed.
Rico Alvarez: Root cause: janitor removed `exporter_payload` before the billing_audit consumer could read it; metering wrote events but some downstream reads were relying on exporter payload to compute vectors. Janitor TTL incorrectly applied to recent objects.
Maya Patel: Remediation options: 1) backfill using archived exporter snapshots (we keep 7d snapshots) to recompute vectors and apply billing adjustments, 2) manual credit, 3) change janitor TTL and accept as credit.
LedgerJanitor: Task: snapshot-restore/backfill/meridian/1807789001 queued by Maya Patel.
Rico Alvarez: I'd prefer backfill + fix janitor TTL config. What's backfill effort?
Maya Patel: Backfill plan: restore relevant exporter snapshots by request_id, recompute billed_vectors, dry-run to CSV. Estimate ~75 minutes compute + ~$55 infra. We'll skip records missing snapshots and surface to finance. Dry-run will include candidate_rows, tokens_delta, est_invoice_delta and checksum.
Gwen Park: Approve dry-run. Schedule during low-traffic window and loop CS. If dry-run token delta deviates >20% from estimate, pause and escalate.
Maya Patel: Scheduling dry-run 2026-05-03T01:00Z. Will post CSV to s3 and summary.
LedgerJanitor: Dry-run completed: candidates=462, tokens=518432, est_invoice_delta=$171 (committed). CSV s3://redwood-backfills/meridian/1807789001-dryrun.csv. Checksums OK.
Rico Alvarez: Looks good. Approve apply. Also push janitor TTL patch to preserve exporter payloads for 72h instead of 48h and add metric janitor_deleted_recent>0 -> page.
Maya Patel: Backfill applied, ledger updated, credit memo CM-46202 created for $171. Audit log saved. Janitor TTL changed and canary running.
Gwen Park: Thanks everyone. Close thread. :white_check_mark:
